title: Edfu and the Temple of Horus
standfirst: Edfu’s Temple of Horus is the most complete temple to survive in Egypt, roof and all. Every cruise between Luxor and Aswan stops here. It is one of the stops in our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: The temple
paragraphs: The Temple of Horus was built in the Ptolemaic period, much later than the temples at Luxor, and it survives almost complete: its great pylon, courtyards and dark inner halls give a clear sense of how an Egyptian temple worked.

sections.heading: The visit
paragraphs: Ships moor at the town, and the temple is a short ride away, often by horse-drawn carriage. Visits are usually early in the morning.

faqs.q: How long is the visit to Edfu?
faqs.a: About two hours, including the ride from the mooring.
Yes, on almost every cruise between Luxor and Aswan, in both directions.
